biography.plain_text: Simon Richard Bolt is an Indonesia-based maritime project owner. long_biography.plain_text:
In Tana Beru, Simon Richard Bolt worked with master shipwright Haji Wahab to turn a designer's plans into a traditional Indonesian phinisi. The build unfolded over several years, with Wahab adjusting parts of the blueprint to follow local construction practice.

The hull moved from Bulukumba to Tanjung Bira for its interior, then to Bali for finishing work. Bolt chose Indonesian materials apart from the engines and prepared the cruiser for long passages across Borneo, Sulawesi, Raja Ampat and Flores. The collaboration joined formal design with the judgement-led methods of South Sulawesi's boatbuilding tradition.

uncertainties.detail: The exact expanded name, Indonesia setting and exact phinisi project align between the input and the republished Kompas report. Search results also identify unrelated Simon Bolts in Australian electricity, Swiss architecture, British retail and European sailing; no evidence connects those careers to Simon Richard Bolt in Indonesia, so none was transferred into this dossier.

The only public source naming Simon Richard Bolt and describing his role is a republished translation of Kompas reporting. Specialist maritime press and the current official charter site corroborate the project's construction and commercial history without naming him. Biography confidence is therefore High rather than Very High.

Direct sources establish a financed maritime construction project, but not the business or assets that produced Bolt's wealth. No positive evidence supports an industry, starting-capital mechanism, current principal holding or relationship to a material wealth-producing asset. All four classifications remain Unknown after considering Shipping & Maritime, Hospitality & Leisure, broad Self-made, Founder, Owner-operator and Investor.

The finished project continues in Indonesian commercial charter, but current public pages do not name Bolt. Booking terms identify Samara Yachting and its subsidiaries or partners as principal without explaining ownership of the vessel or Bolt's current involvement. The dossier therefore treats charter as a historical consequence of the build, not evidence of his present business role.

The translated Kompas report describes Bolt as British and uses male pronouns, but no reliable independent source corroborates nationality, birth particulars or gender. No personal-field proposal is made from that single translated report.

Both biographies focus on independently reported South Sulawesi boatbuilding work and remain complete if the owner no longer holds any yacht. They omit the vessel's name, dimensions, current ownership and technical particulars. The short profile alone includes the later charter purpose; the long profile instead develops craft collaboration, construction stages, material choices and intended passages.

Searches for LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, X, YouTube, TikTok, Wikipedia and personal-site variants found either no match or same-name profiles in unrelated places and industries. The current charter website does not establish that Bolt owns, founded or leads the present business, so it is retained as evidence and not mislabelled as his Company Website.

No active tag is proposed. Traditional boatbuilding and charter are meaningful narrative facts, but the evidence does not establish either as Bolt's defining wealth source, sustained profession or current principal operating role. Assigning a maritime, hospitality or shipbuilding cohort would fail the active catalogue's materiality and click-through tests.
